Alice K: FYI windows-integration CI went red after the lockfile regen on main. Failing in tests/serializers/test_msgpack_serializer.py::test_roundtrip with a msgpack decode mismatch. Full failing log below.

ci-bot: Build windows-integration #4523 — FAILED (1 test failing)

Alice K: stacktrace:
```
> E   AssertionError: Deserialized object != original
E   TypeError: unhashable type: 'bytearray'
File ".../site-packages/msgpack/_unpacker.py", line 412, in unpack
```

Ben R: is this from a direct dependency bump or transitive? I only regenerated poetry.lock to pick up a small constraints fix (didn't manually pin anything).

Sam T: can someone rerun the windows matrix to rule out flakiness? I'll queue a rerun.

ci-bot: Rerun queued: build 4524

Maria L: if rerun still fails, let's bisect the lock. Steps I usually run:
- git fetch origin main && git checkout main
- git bisect start HEAD --last-good <old-lock-commit>
- git bisect run "pip install -e . && pytest tests/serializers/test_msgpack_serializer.py::test_roundtrip -q"

Ben R: rerun failed (4524). @Maria L can you do the bisect? if not I can start it.

Maria L: will run bisect in a couple hours, booking time now — ping me if you need quick repro instructions.

(about 2.5 hours later)

Maria L: bisect result — culprit is a transitive bump: aiomsgpack 0.8.1 -> 0.9.0 (pulled in via async-commune 2.3.0). Repro locally by switching msgpack versions: msgpack==1.0.4 (good) vs msgpack==1.0.5 (bad). Looks like 1.0.5 changed how bytearray is decoded -> becomes bytearray instead of bytes which breaks our equality checks.

Ben R: thanks — opening revert PR to pin aiomsgpack back to 0.8.x and add a test asserting exact type after decode. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/789

Alice K: adding a follow-up card to add lockfile blame info in CI logs (commit ids for lock regen) so next time bisect is faster. :thumbsup:
